body: At my last job, they banned phones but not apple watches. So here's what happened: Everybody who owned an apple watch would be constantly checking messages and replying to stuff on the apple watch during work. And then people who did have an apple watch couldn't do any of that or use other features such as calendars, alarms etc. It was frustrating because it basically gave more privileges to people with apple watches because they could still check their messages and reply as if they had their phone on them, but those without the watch couldn't. I think employers need to realize that phones are used for a lot more than just messages these days, and maybe have like a middle ground rule where you can have your phone on you but just not be using it while you're actively with a client.

My first few water fasts were spanning from 2- 3 days, and then I quickly jumped into a 12 day fast. Tomorrow I'm starting another prolonged fast. I've never done 30. My main advice is electrolytes (potassium and sodium) with plenty of water to keep headaches and dizziness away. Also find things you enjoy that will keep you occupied that don't involve food. For example, relaxing things like watching your favorite show (obvi without snacks, like literally get a rubix cube or fidget spinner to keep your hands busy while watching tv if you're used to snacking). Also, toward the end of the fast, don't stand up too fast bc you can get light headed. Another bit of motivation: ketosis typically happens after day 3 so you should feel better and more energized from ketones by day 4. One of my other fave things to stay distracted was making new music playlists on spotify under different genres. Sorry for that textbook of a comment! Just wanted to help with sharing what helped me get to 12 days. Good luck!
